# DesignComplexSurvival

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/gosukehommaEX/DesignComplexSurvival/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/gosukehommaEX/DesignComplexSurvival/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![License: GPL (>= 2)](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-GPL%20%28%3E%3D%202%29-blue.svg)](https://www.r-project.org/Licenses/)
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/DesignComplexSurvival)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=DesignComplexSurvival)
[![CRAN downloads](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/DesignComplexSurvival)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=DesignComplexSurvival)
[![CRAN downloads total](https://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/grand-total/DesignComplexSurvival)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=DesignComplexSurvival)
[![pkgdown site](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-pkgdown-blue.svg)](https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/gosukehommaEX/DesignComplexSurvival/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/gosukehommaEX/DesignComplexSurvival)
<!-- badges: end -->

DesignComplexSurvival computes the operating characteristics of two-group
time-to-event trials analyzed with the log-rank test, without patient-level
simulation:

* each group follows a multistate model (progression-free, progressed,
  switched, dead, and progression-free after a switch before progression)
  with piecewise constant intensities, covering progression-free survival,
  overall survival and treatment switching before, at or after progression,
  with the post-progression intensities measured from progression or from
  randomization, and the effect of a switch on the death hazard (measured
  on the post-progression clock or from the switch) or as an accelerated
  failure time effect;
* switching may start at a calendar time, for example after an interim
  analysis (for the OS statistic);
* accrual is piecewise uniform (by rates or by proportions), dropout is
  piecewise exponential by group, and PFS may have a censoring of its own
  and be censored at a switch before progression;
* expected events, the mean, variance and covariance of the log-rank
  statistic over calendar time, group sequential bounds by alpha and beta
  spending (binding or non-binding futility), power, type I error, and the
  number of events, sample size, accrual duration or follow-up for a target
  power;
* progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) can be tested
  together with a group sequential fixed-sequence or Bonferroni procedure,
  the latter with recycling of the level after a rejection (Maurer and
  Bretz 2013), with analyses driven by the events of either endpoint or by
  calendar time; the joint distribution of the two log-rank statistics
  gives the power of each endpoint, the probability of rejecting both or at
  least one hypothesis, and the familywise error rate.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("gosukehommaEX/DesignComplexSurvival")
```

## Documentation

The articles on the package website
(<https://gosukehommaEX.github.io/DesignComplexSurvival/>) cover the
workflow of a design, the multistate model and treatment switching, group
sequential designs and the covariance of the statistics, PFS and OS tested
together, switching from a calendar time, and the validation of the package.

## Examples

A delayed treatment effect: the hazard ratio is 1 for 6 months and 0.65
afterwards. The number of events for 90 percent power with interim analyses
at 50 and 75 percent of the events:

```{r example}
library(DesignComplexSurvival)
lam <- log(2) / 12
scn <- ms_scenario(
  control = ms_model(death = lam, dropout = 0.003),
  treatment = ms_model(time = c(0, 6), death = c(lam, 0.65 * lam), dropout = 0.003),
  accrual = ms_accrual(time = c(0, 3), rate = c(10, 30))
)
ms_size(scn, looks = ms_looks("os", fraction = c(0.5, 0.75, 1)),
        test = ms_test(futility = "beta", sf_fut = "HSD", param_fut = -2),
        power = 0.9, solve_for = "events", n = 700)
```

PFS and OS tested together: PFS and OS are exponential in both groups (the
model of Fleischer et al. 2009), with medians of 4 and 12 months in the
control group and 6 and 16 months in the treatment group. PFS is tested at
300 PFS events, where OS is also tested, and OS again at 220 OS events. OS
is tested only after PFS has been rejected (fixed sequence):

```{r example-two}
fl <- ms_scenario(
  control = ms_fleischer(median_pfs = 4, median_os = 12),
  treatment = ms_fleischer(median_pfs = 6, median_os = 16),
  accrual = ms_accrual(rate = 25)
)
ms_power(fl, n = 450,
         looks = ms_looks(c("pfs", "os"), fraction = c(1, 1),
                          test = list(c("pfs", "os"), "os")),
         test = ms_test(endpoints = c("pfs", "os"), mtp = "fixed_sequence"),
         events = c(pfs = 300, os = 220))
```

## Validation

```{r validation-counts, include = FALSE}
judgements <- c("PASS", "EXPLAINED", "FAIL", "INFO")
reproduce <- utils::read.csv("inst/reproduce/results/summary.csv")
validation <- utils::read.csv("inst/validation/results/summary.csv")
count_judgements <- function(x) {
  as.vector(table(factor(x$judgement, levels = judgements)))
}
counts <- rbind(count_judgements(reproduce), count_judgements(validation))
colnames(counts) <- judgements
counts <- data.frame(Folder = c("`inst/reproduce/`", "`inst/validation/`"),
                     counts, Total = rowSums(counts), check.names = FALSE)
n_sources <- length(unique(reproduce$source))
sim_sources <- c("python", "fastsurvival", "python_two", "python_calendar", "danzer")
n_simulated <- length(unique(validation$scenario[validation$source %in% sim_sources]))
n_pweall <- length(unique(validation$scenario[validation$source == "pweall"]))
n_two <- length(unique(validation$scenario[validation$source == "python_two"]))
n_calendar <- length(unique(validation$scenario[validation$source == "python_calendar"]))
n_lrstat <- length(unique(validation$scenario[validation$source == "lrstat_fseqbon"]))
```

The tests compare the results with an independent Python implementation
(`inst/validation/python/`, using matrix exponentials and adaptive
quadrature) and, when the packages are installed, with gsDesign, gsDesign2,
rpact and lrstat.

The scripts in `inst/reproduce/` recompute sample sizes, numbers of events,
analysis times, bounds and powers printed in `r n_sources` sources (articles
and a statistical analysis plan). The scripts in `inst/validation/` compare
the package with patient-level simulations of `r n_simulated` scenarios
(FastSurvival and a Python simulation; PFS and OS analyzed together in
`r n_two` of them, switching from a calendar time in `r n_calendar`), with
the covariance estimator of Danzer et al. (2025) applied to large simulated
trials under the null hypothesis, with the package PWEALL in `r n_pweall`
designs, and with the decisions of `lrstat::fseqbon()` in `r n_lrstat`
designs with recycling of the level. Each folder is run by its
`run_all.R`, which judges every value as PASS (the criterion is met),
EXPLAINED (the criterion is met after a registered explanation, such as an
apparent misprint), FAIL, or INFO (not judged: a published value computed
by a method that the package does not reproduce, or an asymptotic
approximation compared with simulation):

```{r validation-table, echo = FALSE}
knitr::kable(counts, row.names = FALSE)
```

`run_all.R` also multiplies the compared values by 1.1 and checks that the
judgments change as expected. The criteria are described in the
`README.md` of each folder and the registered explanations in its
`explained.csv`. Every compared value is listed with its judgment in
`results/summary.csv`, and `results/summary.md` summarizes the results.
FastSurvival, PWEALL and lrstat (0.3.4 or later) are needed only to rerun
`inst/validation/`.
